clue.text: Suit order to keep in the pink

definitions.meaning: to suit something is to be right or proper for it

definitions.text: order to keep in the pink
definitions.meaning: an instruction to stay in good health, read as a two-word command telling someone to stay healthy

explanation.surface: A tailor is told to keep a pink suit order in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' is an old idiom for being in good health, so the second half is a command to stay healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are appropriate or seemly are said to suit, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Work I took in as a means of escape

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
to take in food is to eat it, so took in gives ATE

explanation.surface: A worker says that taking on a job was his way of getting away from things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is figurative: a drug that dulls the senses offers escape from reality.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic drug brings oblivion, which people use to flee from pain or reality.

clue.text: Having resisted, took a prominent position

definitions.meaning: to hold out against pressure, past tense, as in refusing to give in
was conspicuous, rose above the rest in plain view

explanation.surface: Someone who refused to give way ended up in a conspicuous place.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both held firm against opposition and was conspicuous, two separate senses.

clue.text: 20 across with O.T. character in a musical

parts.note: the answer to 20 across means arrived, which is also what came means
Lot is a figure in the Old Testament, Abraham's nephew

explanation.surface: A cross-reference and an Old Testament figure combine to make a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The 20 across answer, used in its sense of having arrived, gives CAME; O.T. is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerner and Loewe wrote a stage show about King Arthur's court with this title.

clue.text: Fish struggle awkwardly

definitions.meaning: a flatfish of the plaice family
to move clumsily or flail about, as in deep mud

explanation.surface: A fish out of water thrashes about clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flatfish and also means to thrash or stumble clumsily.

clue.text: Military command for further supplies?

definitions.meaning: a drill instruction telling soldiers to lower their rifles to the ground by their side
read literally, a request to send more weapons

explanation.surface: An officer barks an order asking for more provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: placing an order for more weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a parade-ground drill word of command, and literally a requisition for weapons.

clue.text: Maintain in a safe anchorage to ward off danger

definitions.meaning: read literally, to hold a ship moored in a sheltered inlet of the sea
to hold a threat at a distance, fending it off

explanation.surface: A captain keeps the ship in harbour so it avoids peril.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the idiom literally: a bay is a sheltered stretch of coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to hold off a threat, and literally to hold something in a sheltered inlet.

clue.text: Girl in Ireland

definitions.meaning: a girl's first name
a county in the west of Ireland, on the Atlantic coast

explanation.surface: A young woman lives on the Emerald Isle.
explanation.walkthrough: CLARE is a county in the west of Ireland, as well as a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a female first name and a county on Ireland's west coast.

clue.text: Lake in winter I exclude

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found running inside the following words

explanation.surface: A lake is something I shut out of my life during the cold months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you to look inside 'winter I exclude', where the letters run across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America bears this name, so it is an example.

clue.text: Ship produced on stage

parts.note: a vessel that exists only in a theatrical production, the title of a comic opera about the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A vessel is brought out in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, the 'ship' of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta is named after a fictional naval vessel, staged rather than sailed.

clue.text: Directed to utter defeat?

definitions.meaning: sent along a particular path, past tense
put to complete defeat, as an army beaten and scattered

explanation.surface: Troops were sent off only to suffer a crushing loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'booted', the other with 'shouted'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelling serves both for sent along a path and for crushingly beaten in battle.

clue.text: Much-admired person is nothing in the end to her

indicators.note: placed at the close of the preceding word, so the zero comes last

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A celebrity counts for nothing, as far as she is concerned in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end to' sets the O after HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idolised for courage or achievement is exactly what this word describes.

clue.text: Use a purple patch and get into the red

definitions.meaning: to describe something in overwrought, florid terms, exaggerating it
to take more from a bank account than it holds

explanation.surface: Someone splashes out on purple and ends up in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: A purple patch is an over-ornate passage of writing; 'in the red' means in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to exaggerate in description and to withdraw more than an account holds.

clue.text: It is queer to be reformed of necessity

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase meaning necessary, matching the adjective

indicators.note: to be reformed is to be made over in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists that oddness must be corrected, as a matter of need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reformed' rearranges the nine letters of IT IS QUEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needed or essential is required, which is what the adjective expresses.

clue.text: Full up inside

parts.note: describes a stomach filled to capacity after a big meal

explanation.surface: After dinner one feels stuffed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means filled, especially sated with food, as a well-fed diner is.

clue.text: Hang around, that is, for underwear

parts.note: to stay on, loiter, is to linger
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Loitering about, apparently, in the interests of undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: IE stands for id est, 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's undergarments collectively go by this French-derived word.

clue.text: Knotted threadwork made with care, mam

indicators.note: made signals that the following letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A mother's lacy knotwork has been produced with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges CARE and MAM, seven letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: This craft produces decorative fabric by knotting cord or thread in patterns.

clue.text: Everything having been considered, in seemingly illogical position

definitions.meaning: when all is weighed up, in the end
read literally, placed behind everything, which cannot really happen

explanation.surface: Weighing everything up, something seems to be in a strange place.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, being behind everything is a paradox, since nothing can come after the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means when everything is weighed up, and literally behind every single thing.

clue.text: Gourmet

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held only as 'Gourmet' (7): a bare definition with no wordplay; the rest of the clue appears lost in OCR and no scan is available.

clue.text: Snub having arrived

definitions.meaning: short and pointing upward, as a snub nose is
showed up, appeared at an event

explanation.surface: A guest gets cold-shouldered on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snub' is the adjective, as in a snub nose, not the verb meaning to slight.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose tilts upward, and to show up is to arrive.

clue.text: "If hopes were ——s, fears may be liars" (Clough)

definitions.text: "If hopes were ——s, fears may be liars" (Clough)

parts.words: "If hopes were ——s, fears may be liars" (Clough)
parts.note: a line from Arthur Hugh Clough's poem Say not the struggle nought availeth, missing a word for those who are deceived

explanation.surface: A Victorian poet's line with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is Clough's 'Say not the struggle nought availeth'; the gap needs a word for people who are fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means people who are fooled or deceived, balancing liars in the line.

clue.text: Fowl or a set of three

definitions.meaning: a seabird related to the gull
a trio or group of three, as in a lottery win on three numbers

explanation.surface: Birds are counted out in threes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a seabird and also an old term for a trio of things.

clue.text: Prize for an upset artist

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: A competition award is offered to a painter who is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DRAWER round; in a down clue the word is turned bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given in recognition of a win or achievement is a synonym for a prize.

clue.text: Share out a considerable quantity as I hear

indicators.note: as I hear tells the solver the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a lot means a great deal, a considerable quantity

explanation.surface: Someone has heard they will be dividing up a large amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as I hear' signals that A LOT sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute portions to each party is to apportion them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Unconscious while huntsman returns

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was walking'

indicators.note: returns means the name is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: John Peel is the huntsman of the old English song D'ye ken John Peel

explanation.surface: A hunter comes back home while someone lies insensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' signals the reversal; 'huntsman' looks generic but points to one man. John Peel is the Cumbrian huntsman of the folk song 'D'ye ken John Peel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is not awake to their surroundings, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Grain barrier in England

parts.note: corn is a general word for cereal grain

explanation.surface: A wall built around a cornfield somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNWALL is the county at England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-westernmost county lies within England, so the phrase describes its location.

clue.text: Flight recommended for those with mounting ambitions

definitions.text: Flight recommended for those with mounting ambitions

parts.words: Flight recommended for those with mounting ambitions
parts.note: reads as advice on air travel for climbers, but a flight here is a series of steps one goes up

explanation.surface: A travel tip for aspiring climbers about which plane to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel, but a flight is also a set of steps, and 'mounting' means climbing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step in a flight, which people climb when ascending, fits the cryptic image.

clue.text: Setting for a cross-examination in a restaurant?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a room where someone is questioned hard
an eating place serving grilled food

explanation.surface: A suspect is questioned harshly over dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: To grill someone is to question them relentlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: It names an eatery specialising in grilled meat, and literally a room for intense questioning.
